notes: rosbuild ROS 1 package (manifest.xml has no version element, so manifest_version is null). All six packet elements are consumed by library/src/ros/android/views/TurtlebotDashboard.java; the package provides none of them, so declares and not_declared are empty. TurtlebotDashboard is the default dashboard when the parameter robot/dashboard/class_name is absent (library/src/ros/android/util/Dashboard.java:151-159). Topic name: the code writes the relative name "diagnostics_agg" (recorded verbatim in references); the node's parent resolver uses namespace "/" with an empty remapping map (library/src/ros/android/util/MasterChooser.java:215-217, applied at :230), so it resolves to /diagnostics_agg, the packet element. frame is 'none' for every port: diagnostics carry no spatial meaning and the code never reads the DiagnosticArray header or frame_id. units null: KeyValue.value is a string; the code parses values under the keys "Charge (Ah)", "Capacity (Ah)" and "Current (A)" (TurtlebotDashboard.java:275-276, 288), so the units appear only in key strings, not as a declared unit of the field. Status names matched: "/Power System/Battery", "/Power System/Laptop Battery", "/Mode/Operating Mode" (lines 158, 161, 164). QoS null throughout (ROS 1); no rate set. definition_id null for all ports: ros_distro is null in the packet, so there is no release tag from which dependency definitions may be fetched, and the snapshot contains no .msg/.srv/.action/.idl files (appman.rosinstall names /opt/ros/electric, but that file was not used to choose a tag). Other diagnostic_msgs elements the code uses but that are not packet elements: field DiagnosticArray.status (line 157), field DiagnosticStatus.message (line 165), msg DiagnosticStatus and msg KeyValue (imports lines 56-57); they are not listed in references. Pr2Dashboard.java imports DiagnosticArray, DiagnosticStatus and KeyValue (lines 58-60) but never uses them; it subscribes to dashboard_agg (pr2_msgs/DashboardState) instead. perm_requires records Android platform permissions from library/AndroidManifest.xml, not ROS-level permissions. WiFiChecker.java contains WiFi reconnection logic for joining the robot network; it is not a recovery declaration for these interface elements, so recovery is recorded as absent.
